title: The Château and the Transmitter: Guattari, La Borde, and the Twenty-Two Years with Deleuze
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: The Oise, the Party, and the Couch

stops.name: Villeneuve-lès-Sablons, birth in the Oise
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day. The pin is corrected: French Wikipedia gives the commune at 49 deg 14 min 15 sec N, 2 deg 04 min 39 sec E; the pair 49.2833 / 1.9167 that circulates in gathered material lands about 13 km west-northwest, in open country
stops.campa: Pierre-Félix Guattari is born on the thirtieth of March in a rural bourg of the Oise, some fifty kilometres from Paris and twenty-six from Beauvais, outside any urban unit the census recognizes. English accounts will later call the place a working-class suburb of northwest Paris; the French record calls it farmland with a church in it. He will spend his working life arguing that the family is not the first thing, that desire is manufactured socially long before it is manufactured at home. Almost nothing else about the household is documented in anything reachable.
suggested_refs: Civil registers of Villeneuve-lès-Sablons, Oise, for March 1930
A source for the claim, unsupported in either Wikipedia article, that his father Louis founded the Monbana chocolate company

stops.name: Paris, the school of Fernand Oury
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year 1945 by French Wikipedia's 'Jean Oury'; month and day defaulted. The specific school is not named in any source reached, and the pin is a generic Paris coordinate
stops.campa: He is fifteen, a pupil of Fernand Oury, the schoolteacher assembling a pedagogy out of Freinet's printing press and the cooperative classroom. Through Fernand he meets the brother, Jean Oury, who is going into psychiatry. The French record fixes the meeting here, in Paris, in this year. A widely repeated version puts it eight years later at a clinic in the Loire valley instead, which would have two men meeting for the first time who were by then old acquaintances. Forty-seven years after this classroom, the two of them are still working in the same building.
suggested_refs: Fernand Oury's papers on institutional pedagogy, for the classroom Guattari sat in
Any source naming the Paris school where the Ourys and Guattari met in 1945

stops.name: Paris, the Party and the turn to its left
stops.date_confidence: reconstructed. Both language editions record membership of the French Communist Party through his youth and early twenties, and teenage Trotskyist activism preceding the psychiatric career, neither with dates. The year 1948 is a placement inside that span and the month and day are defaulted
stops.campa: He is a member of the French Communist Party and, at the same time or very soon after, a Trotskyist: the postwar itinerary of a whole generation of Paris students who pass through the Party's structures and break out to its left. No source reached gives dates for either, and none names a section, a cell or a paper. What the record does give is the order of operations: the militancy comes first, the psychiatry second. He is organizing before he ever sets foot on a ward. Whether he is eighteen here or twenty-three, the record will not say.
suggested_refs: PCF section records for the Paris student cells of the late 1940s
Any dated account of Guattari's teenage Trotskyist activity

stops.name: Paris, the University and the analysis with Lacan
stops.date_confidence: attested for the early 1950s by English Wikipedia; the year 1951 and the month and day are placements inside that span. The pin is a generic Paris coordinate, no consulting-room address having been reached
stops.campa: He enrols at the University of Paris and goes onto the couch of Jacques Lacan, who is at this moment rebuilding French psychoanalysis around the signifier. The analysis runs for years. Guattari is not only an analysand: he is taken into the circle, something close to an apprentice, and he stays inside the institution long enough to learn where all its joints are. Twenty-one years later he publishes a book treating the consulting room as a machine for fitting people to capitalism. The analysis itself is undated in everything reached, and no consulting-room address survives either.
suggested_refs: Registers of the Faculté de Paris for Guattari's enrolment
The Anti-Oedipus Papers (Semiotext(e), 2006), his preparatory notebooks, for the internal record of the break with Lacanian orthodoxy

stops.name: Hôpital Sainte-Anne, amphithéâtre Magnan: the seminar
stops.date_confidence: attested that Lacan's public seminar opened at Sainte-Anne in 1953 and ran there until 1963-64, moving to the rue d'Ulm in January 1964 and to the Faculté de Droit in 1969; the span '1952-1969' attached to Sainte-Anne in gathered material is wrong. Month set to November by convention for the first session, day defaulted. The pin is the corpus value carried by artaud.journey.json and jacques_lacan.journey.json, which records three competing Sainte-Anne pairs and does not resolve them
stops.campa: Lacan opens his teaching to anyone who will come, in the Magnan amphitheatre of the hospital where he trained, one subject a year, a year at a time. Guattari is in the room. Analysts come first, then philosophers, then people with no professional business there at all. He sits through the years in which the unconscious is declared to be structured like a language, taking notes he will spend his forties dismantling. There is no expulsion here and no public rupture later. He keeps an analytic practice of his own to the end of his life.
suggested_refs: Le Séminaire, livres I-X, the Sainte-Anne years, for what Guattari sat through
sources: jacques_lacan.journey.json (Sainte-Anne pin and the record of competing coordinates)

stops.name: Saumery, the clinic in the Loir-et-Cher
stops.date_confidence: reconstructed. Jean Oury was médecin-chef at the Clinique de Saumery from 1949 until he left in 1953 to found La Borde; Guattari's visits fall inside that span but no source reached dates one, and the month is inferred. No source reached gives coordinates for Saumery, and the pin is approximate for the Loir-et-Cher
stops.campa: Jean Oury is running a clinic at Saumery, in the Loir-et-Cher, and Guattari comes down from Paris to see what he is doing with it. What Oury is doing comes out of Saint-Alban in the Lozère, where François Tosquelles had spent the war treating the asylum itself as the patient. The proposition is that an institution is a machine which either produces madness or works against it, and that no analysis of a person is worth much if the ward is left out of the account. Guattari arrives already convinced and stays to learn the machinery. In 1953 Oury leaves Saumery for a château at Cour-Cheverny.
suggested_refs: The Château de Saumery at Huisseau-sur-Cosson, for a coordinate and for the clinic's records 1949-1953
Tosquelles at Saint-Alban, 1940-1945, the origin of the method Oury carried north

stops.name: Clinique de La Borde, Cour-Cheverny: he follows Oury
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year Guattari arrives; month and day defaulted. The clinic itself was founded by Oury alone on 3 April 1953 with 33 patients and accredited that June for 29 beds, so the common formula 'Oury founds La Borde in 1955 and Guattari follows him' conflates two events two years apart. French Wikipedia's Guattari article calls him a 1953 co-founder; its own article on the clinic credits Oury alone and does not name him. The contradiction is recorded, not silently resolved. The pin is inherited byte-identical from gilles_deleuze.journey.json
stops.campa: Oury has taken a decaying château north of Cour-Cheverny and filled it with the thirty-three patients he brought with him. Guattari comes two years later and never really leaves. At La Borde the kitchen rota, the newspaper, the accounts and the summer play are run by whoever is there, and the line between staff and inmate is kept deliberately unstable so that nobody settles into a role. He will work here for thirty-seven years, out of a suitcase in Paris and a room in the Loir-et-Cher.
suggested_refs: La Borde's own accounts of the 1953 opening, cited by Oury: 33 patients, Social Security accreditation June 1953, 29 beds
sources: gilles_deleuze.journey.json (La Borde pin, and the stop recording that no source places Deleuze himself on the premises)
nick_land.journey.json (La Borde named as Guattari's clinic, staff and patient roles deliberately rotated)

stops.name: Clinique de La Borde: the administrative direction
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1957 by French Wikipedia's 'Jean Oury'; month and day defaulted. English Wikipedia dates his following Oury to 1955 and says nothing of the appointment. The two accounts are compatible but no single source states both, and the difference is left open
stops.campa: Oury asks him to take the administration. It is not a medical post; Guattari has no medical degree and never will. What he has is the books, the rotas, the payroll and the permanent argument about who cleans what. He holds the job for decades. The theory of institutions he publishes later comes off that desk: how a hundred-bed clinic stays solvent while the people committed to it decide how the laundry runs. The English-language accounts date his arrival to 1955 and pass over the appointment entirely.
suggested_refs: La Borde's administrative records for the years of Guattari's direction

stops.name: Clinique de La Borde: the working group and the grid
stops.date_confidence: attested for the GTPSI period around 1960 to 1966; the year is a placement inside that span and the month and day are defaulted. The Association pour la Psychothérapie Institutionnelle was formally constituted in November 1965
stops.campa: The Groupe de Travail de Psychothérapie et de Sociothérapie Institutionnelles meets: Oury, Guattari, François Tosquelles and the rest of the movement that came out of Saint-Alban. They call the practice institutional psychotherapy and they mean it flatly, that the hospital is the thing under treatment. Guattari's own contribution is the grid, the rotating schedule that prevents any function in the clinic from hardening onto any one body. It is a duty roster and it is a theory of who is permitted to be what. In November 1965 the group is constituted as an association.
suggested_refs: Surviving copies of the La Borde grid, the rotating task schedule
Nicolas Philibert, La Moindre des choses (1997), filmed at La Borde, for the annual play and the working method after Guattari's death

stops.name: Paris, the offices of La Voie Communiste
stops.date_confidence: attested that Guattari edited and wrote for the paper across roughly 1955 to 1965; the year is a placement mid-run and the month and day are defaulted. No editorial address is documented in any source reached, and the pin is a generic Paris coordinate
stops.campa: He edits La Voie Communiste, a far-left paper of Trotskyist tendency, for about ten years. On Fridays he is on a train to the Loir-et-Cher to argue about the laundry rota; in Paris he is producing copy against the Party he grew up in and against the war in Algeria. Nobody at the clinic finds the combination strange, and neither does he. This is where the working habit sets: organizing several things at once and publishing out of all of them. Where the paper was actually put together, which street, which room, is not recorded in anything reached. It folds around 1965.
suggested_refs: Runs of La Voie Communiste, 1955-1965, for the articles signed by Guattari

stops.name: Paris, the FGERI
stops.date_confidence: attested for the FGERI founding in 1965; month and day defaulted. The journal Recherches, often attached to this date, did not appear until 1966 and is more precisely the organ of CERFI, a distinct body founded in 1967
stops.campa: The Fédération des Groupes d'Études et de Recherches Institutionnelles is founded, and with it his method leaves the ward. Psychiatrists, architects, economists, film-makers, teachers and town planners are put in the same room on the proposition that the analysis of an institution is one operation whatever the institution happens to be. After this he stops distinguishing between a clinic, a school and a housing estate, and he never starts again. The journal Recherches follows the next year.
suggested_refs: The founding statutes of the FGERI, 1965
Recherches, 49 issues, 1966 to 1982-83

stops.name: Paris, OSARLA and the first Latin American thread
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year by English Wikipedia; month and day defaulted. No further detail on the organization, its membership or its activity was reached this session, and the pin is a generic Paris coordinate
stops.campa: Guattari appears among the founders of OSARLA, a solidarity organization turned toward Latin America. What the record reached this session gives is the name and the year, and then a wall: no membership list, no address, no bulletin, not one action anybody can date. It is the earliest documented thread between him and a continent that will read him harder than Europe does, and São Paulo is fifteen years off. Whether he did anything in it beyond lending a signature cannot be established from here.
suggested_refs: Any surviving OSARLA bulletin or statute naming its founders

stops.name: Paris, CERFI
stops.date_confidence: attested for the founding year 1967 by French Wikipedia's dedicated CERFI article, which gives the dissolution as 1987; the month is inferred and the day defaulted. English Wikipedia's 1970 and the 1965 given elsewhere are both unsupported by the specialist entry, 1965 belonging to FGERI. No CERFI address is documented and the pin is generic Paris
stops.campa: He founds the Centre d'Études, de Recherches et de Formation Institutionnelles, which takes state research money to study hospitals, new towns, collective facilities, the whole equipment of a country. CERFI runs the surveys the ministries pay for and publishes Recherches out of the proceeds, forty-nine issues between 1966 and the early eighties. A militant collective living off government urbanism contracts is a strange machine to have built on purpose. The centre is dissolved in 1987, twenty years after it opens.
suggested_refs: CERFI's commissioned reports for the French ministries, 1967-1987
Recherches no. 13, 'Généalogie du capital: les équipements du pouvoir'

stops.name: Nanterre, the Twenty-Second of March
stops.date_confidence: attested for Nanterre as the epicentre of the March 22 Movement and of May 1968, and for Guattari's participation in the movement and in the events. The pin is corrected: French Wikipedia gives Université Paris-Nanterre at 48.90394 N, 2.21378 E, where the pair 48.8926 / 2.2136 in gathered material falls about 1.3 km south of the campus
stops.campa: The occupation at Nanterre begins the sequence that becomes May. Guattari is thirty-eight, a clinic administrator with a decade of newspaper work behind him, and he is in it up to the neck. He meets Daniel Cohn-Bendit, Jean-Jacques Lebel, Julian Beck of the Living Theatre; the countercultural wing takes him in as readily as the Trotskyists had a decade before. He comes out of it with a list of names and the conviction that the thing failed for want of a theory of desire. The barricades go up in Paris in May and come down in June.
suggested_refs: Documents of the Mouvement du 22 Mars, Nanterre, 1968

stops.name: Vincennes: the campus built for what the state cannot govern
stops.date_confidence: attested that the experimental campus opened in the Bois de Vincennes in January 1969 and that Deleuze was appointed to its philosophy department that year, Foucault having suggested the hiring. Guattari held no post there in 1969 and the two never ran joint seminars on the campus; the trailing claim that Vincennes was a hub for their joint seminars is dropped. English accounts placing their first meeting here are tradition, not attestation. No source reached supplies coordinates for the razed campus, and the pin is the corpus value carried by gilles_deleuze.journey.json
stops.campa: The prefabricated blocks go up in the Bois de Vincennes to absorb the students the state cannot otherwise place after May. Michel Foucault is handed the philosophy department and staffs it with the militant left, bringing in Gilles Deleuze at last. Guattari has no post here and never will have one. The English accounts that put his first meeting with Deleuze on this campus are repeating a story rather than a document. He comes as a visitor. The doors of the lecture rooms are not locked, and half of Paris walks in through them.
suggested_refs: Founding appointment lists of the Vincennes philosophy department, 1968-1969
Photographs of the campus before its demolition, 27-29 August 1980

stops.name: Paris: the meeting with Gilles Deleuze
stops.date_confidence: contested, and inherited as contested. The introduction through the La Borde psychiatrist Jean-Pierre Muyard is well attested; the site is not. English accounts say the Vincennes campus, Dosse's dual biography says Deleuze's country house in the Limousin during the convalescence after his 1968 lung surgery, and a third version puts it at a Paris apartment on no evidence reached this session. No primary Dosse text was reachable. The pin is a placeholder inherited byte-identical from gilles_deleuze.journey.json, which records the same conflict on the same coordinate. Month per Dosse's June, day defaulted
stops.campa: Jean-Pierre Muyard, a psychiatrist from La Borde, puts the two men together. Guattari is thirty-nine and has published almost nothing under his own name; Deleuze is forty-four, has written a shelf of books on other philosophers, and has recently lost a lung. Twenty-two years and four books follow, and neither signature can afterwards be pulled out of the text by anyone, the two authors included. The sources cannot agree on the room they sat down in. This pin marks a site nobody has established.
suggested_refs: Correspondence between Deleuze and Guattari from 1969, which would fix the date and the place
François Dosse, Gilles Deleuze et Félix Guattari: biographie croisée (2007), unreachable this session
sources: gilles_deleuze.journey.json (stop 'Paris: the meeting with Felix Guattari', pin and contested-site flag inherited)

stops.name: Saint-Léonard-de-Noblat: the house in the Limousin
stops.date_confidence: reconstructed throughout. Deleuze's family tie to this Haute-Vienne town is documented mainly by his burial there in 1995; Dosse places the June 1969 first meeting at the country house during the convalescence, and the secondary literature describes repeated working visits through the 1970s. No source fetched this session confirms a single dated visit by Guattari, and the year is a placeholder. Pin inherited from gilles_deleuze.journey.json
stops.campa: Deleuze's family keeps a house in this town of five thousand people in the Haute-Vienne, and the tradition is that Guattari comes down from Paris again and again through the seventies, for days at a stretch, to write. The method is not correspondence. It is two men in a room, the drafts crossed out in both hands until neither can say afterwards whose sentence a sentence was. No dated visit is documented in anything reached this session. The tradition is strong and the paper trail is empty. How many times he came, and in which years, nobody has shown.
stops.quote: The body without organs is an egg: it is crisscrossed with axes and thresholds, with latitudes and longitudes and geodesic lines, traversed by gradients marking the transitions and the becomings, the destinations of the subject developing along these particular vectors.
stops.quote_source: Deleuze and Guattari, Anti-Oedipus, trans. Hurley, Seem and Lane (Viking, 1977), ch. 1 'The Desiring-Machines', p. 19. Verified verbatim against the PDF; gathered material misattributed the passage to ch. 2
suggested_refs: Antonin Artaud, 'Pour en finir avec le jugement de dieu' (1947), commonly named as the source of the phrase 'body without organs', to verify against artaud.journey.json
Any dated record of Guattari's visits to the Limousin house
sources: gilles_deleuze.journey.json (Saint-Leonard-de-Noblat pin; the Limousin convalescence stop)

stops.name: Éditions de Minuit, rue Bernard-Palissy: L'Anti-Œdipe
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year 1972 and the publisher; month inferred and day defaulted. Minuit has been at 7 rue Bernard-Palissy in the sixth arrondissement since 1951 per French Wikipedia. Pin inherited byte-identical from gilles_deleuze.journey.json. Michel Foucault's preface belongs to the 1977 American edition and not to this one
stops.campa: Capitalisme et schizophrénie, volume one. Desire produces rather than lacks; the unconscious is a factory and not a theatre; the family triangle that psychoanalysis keeps finding at the bottom of everyone is not the origin of anything but an instrument for making the desire of a whole society private and small. It is an assault on Lacan's institution written by a man Lacan analysed, and it sells like a novel. The question it takes up is Wilhelm Reich's, why the masses desired fascism, and it refuses Reich's answer along with everybody else's.
stops.quote: It is at work everywhere, functioning smoothly at times, at other times in fits and starts. It breathes, it heats, it eats. It shits and fucks. What a mistake to have ever said the id.
stops.quote_source: Deleuze and Guattari, Anti-Oedipus, trans. Hurley, Seem and Lane (Viking, 1977), opening lines of ch. 1 'Desiring-Production'. Read directly from the PDF
suggested_refs: L'Anti-Œdipe, Éditions de Minuit, 1972, first printing

stops.name: Paris, the court and the three billion perverts
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year of the prosecution by English Wikipedia; month and day defaulted. The issue is Recherches no. 12, 'Trois milliards de pervers: grande encyclopédie des homosexualités'. No courtroom address was reached and the pin is generic Paris
stops.campa: Recherches devotes an issue to homosexuality and the state prosecutes its publication director for outrage to public decency. Guattari is fined and the copies are ordered destroyed. He is forty-three, has a bestseller in the shops arguing that desire is a productive force the social order must keep repressed, and is standing in a French courtroom being fined for printing what people desire. What the fine came to, and whether every copy was found and burned, is not recorded in anything reached this session.
stops.quote: The truth is that sexuality is everywhere: the way a bureaucrat fondles his records, a judge administers justice, a businessman causes money to circulate; the way the bourgeoisie fucks the proletariat; and so on.
stops.quote_source: Deleuze and Guattari, Anti-Oedipus, trans. Hurley, Seem and Lane (Viking, 1977), ch. 4 'Introduction to Schizoanalysis', p. 293. Verified verbatim against the PDF; gathered material misattributed the passage to ch. 2
suggested_refs: Recherches no. 12, 'Trois milliards de pervers' (March 1973), and the court order for its destruction

stops.name: Éditions de Minuit: Kafka, pour une littérature mineure
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year of publication and the publisher; month and day defaulted. Pin inherited from gilles_deleuze.journey.json
stops.campa: The second joint book is short and it is about Kafka. They read him not as the anguished son of a terrible father but as a comic writer building machines: the burrow, the trial, the castle, the letters to Felice working as an apparatus for holding a woman at a usable distance. A minor literature in their sense is not a small one. It is a literature written inside a major language by people the language does not fit, where every private sentence is immediately political because there is no private room to keep it in.
suggested_refs: Kafka: pour une littérature mineure, Éditions de Minuit, 1975, first edition

stops.name: Columbia University, New York: Schizo-Culture
stops.date_confidence: attested to November 1975 by English Wikipedia's 'Sylvère Lotringer'; the day is defaulted
stops.campa: Sylvère Lotringer gets Guattari, Michel Foucault and R. D. Laing onto one programme in Manhattan and more than two thousand people turn up. It does not go smoothly. Later accounts describe a run of confrontations between the platform and the floor, speakers accused from the audience of being police, panels collapsing into shouting. American theory will date its schizoanalytic turn from this room, which is not what anyone present thought was happening. In the room, Guattari's French is being translated at speed and his politics worse.
stops.quote: If desire is repressed, it is because every position of desire, no matter how small, is capable of calling into question the established order of a society: not that desire is asocial; on the contrary. But it is explosive; there is no desiring-machine capable of being assembled without demolishing entire social sectors.
stops.quote_source: Deleuze and Guattari, Anti-Oedipus, trans. Hurley, Seem and Lane (Viking, 1977). Verified verbatim against the PDF
suggested_refs: Schizo-Culture: The Event 1975 (Semiotext(e), 2013), the published record of the conference

stops.name: Éditions de Minuit: Rhizome
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year of publication; month and day defaulted. The text is later folded in as the introduction to Mille Plateaux, which is where the verified quotation on this stop is read from. Pin inherited from gilles_deleuze.journey.json
stops.campa: A pamphlet of a few dozen pages appears with both names on it, arguing that thought has been organized as a tree for as long as anyone can remember: one root, one trunk, a hierarchy of branches, a single origin and a single direction. Against it they set the rhizome, which can be entered at any point, broken anywhere and restarted from any fragment, and which has no centre to defend. It becomes the most quoted thing either man ever writes. Four years later the pamphlet is folded in as the opening of a much larger book.
stops.quote: We're tired of trees. We should stop believing in trees, roots, and radicles. They've made us suffer too much. All of arborescent culture is founded on them, from biology to linguistics.
stops.quote_source: Deleuze and Guattari, A Thousand Plateaus, trans. Brian Massumi (University of Minnesota Press, 1987), ch. 1 'Rhizome'. Verified verbatim against the Massumi PDF
suggested_refs: Rhizome: introduction, Éditions de Minuit, 1976, the standalone pamphlet

stops.name: Paris, La Révolution moléculaire
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year of publication; month and day defaulted. The pin is a generic Paris coordinate
stops.campa: Under his own name alone he collects a decade of articles and calls the result molecular revolution. Politics conducted at the scale of parties and classes, which he calls molar, keeps missing what actually moves: the ward, the newspaper, the couple, the transmitter, the classroom. The molar is assembled out of the molecular, he argues, and can therefore be taken apart there. That is a harder proposition to build an organization around than the one it replaces. Éditions Recherches publishes the book in 1977.
suggested_refs: La Révolution moléculaire (Éditions Recherches, 1977), first edition

stops.name: New York, Viking Penguin: Anti-Oedipus in English
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year, the translators and the publisher; the month is inferred and the day defaulted. No address for Viking Penguin was reached and the pin is a generic New York coordinate. Foucault's preface belongs to this edition, not to the 1972 French one; the book is later reissued by the University of Minnesota Press
stops.campa: Robert Hurley, Mark Seem and Helen Lane put the book into English and Viking Penguin publishes it five years after Minuit. Michel Foucault writes the preface, and what he offers is not a summary but a use: read it as a manual for living, an ethics against the fascism inside the head that makes people want the very thing that dominates them. The American reception starts here, and it is chiefly a reception of Deleuze. The phrase Foucault offers as an alternative title travels further than most of the book does: "an Introduction to the Non-Fascist Life."
stops.quote: Paying a modest tribute to Saint Francis de Sales, one might say that Anti-Oedipus is an Introduction to the Non-Fascist Life.
stops.quote_source: Michel Foucault, preface to Anti-Oedipus, trans. Robert Hurley (Viking, 1977 English edition). Verified verbatim against the PDF
suggested_refs: Anti-Oedipus, Viking Penguin, 1977, first English edition with Foucault's preface
sources: nick_land.journey.json (the Warwick-era reassembly of this text)

segments.name: Italy, the Free Radios, the Raids

stops.name: Bologna, the preface for Radio Alice
stops.date_confidence: attested that Guattari wrote the preface to the French edition of Radio Alice, radio libre; no source reached fixes the month, which is defaulted along with the day. The station was closed by police in March 1977
stops.campa: Radio Alice broadcasts out of Bologna until the police come through the studio door in March and the last minutes go out live on air. Guattari writes the preface to the book the collective makes out of the wreckage. He has been arguing for years that a transmitter is a desiring-machine and that the state grasps this more quickly than the left does; here is a room in Italy where somebody built one, and here are the tapes of it being switched off. He aligns himself in print with Autonomia in the month Autonomia becomes a criminal category.
suggested_refs: Collectif A/traverso, Radio Alice, radio libre (Jean-Pierre Delarge, 1977), with Guattari's preface

stops.name: Paris, the manifesto against repression in Italy
stops.date_confidence: attested to July 1977 by Italian Wikipedia's record of the Manifesto contro la repressione, signed by 28 intellectuals including Sartre, Beauvoir, Foucault, Barthes, Sollers, Deleuze and Guattari; the day is defaulted. Gathered material dated the appeal to November and described it as protesting Antonio Negri's imprisonment, which is impossible: Negri was not arrested until 7 April 1979. The Negri clause is removed
stops.campa: Twenty-eight French intellectuals sign an appeal against the Italian crackdown. Sartre and Beauvoir sign it, Michel Foucault and Roland Barthes sign it, Deleuze and Guattari sign it. The occasion is the killing of the student Francesco Lorusso in Bologna in March and the wave of arrests that follows it, not the Negri case, which does not yet exist. Guattari's Italian involvement runs a decade from this document forward, and it has a price: the French police start taking an interest in his address.
suggested_refs: The July 1977 Manifesto contro la repressione and its full list of 28 signatories

stops.name: Bologna, the conference against repression
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The September 1977 international conference against repression in Bologna is well documented as an event, but no dedicated source page placing Guattari in the hall could be located or fetched this session; attempted URLs returned 404. The day is defaulted and the attendance is unverified
stops.campa: Tens of thousands come to Bologna in September for the international conference against repression, three days of assembly that the Italian left will spend the following twenty years arguing about. Guattari is reported to have been there. No source reached this session puts him in the hall, and the report rests on recollection alone. It is the kind of gap that closes the moment somebody produces a programme with his name on it, and until then the claim stands without a document under it.
suggested_refs: The printed programme and speaker list of the Bologna convegno contro la repressione, 23-25 September 1977

stops.name: Paris, CINEL
stops.date_confidence: attested for the CINEL period 1977 to 1981 by French Wikipedia, and for Gisèle Donnard's co-direction; the month is inferred and the day defaulted. No CINEL address was reached and the pin is generic Paris
stops.campa: The Centre d'Initiative pour de Nouveaux Espaces de Liberté runs out of Paris with Gisèle Donnard: solidarity with the Italian autonomists, legal support, asylum, free radio, a rock festival called Antibrouille in 1978, a radio conference under the name ALFREDO. New spaces of freedom is his own phrase and he means it administratively as much as poetically. Somebody has to find the money, the lawyer and the frequency, and he has been doing that job at the clinic since he was twenty-five.

stops.name: Paris, the flat searched
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year by French Wikipedia; month and day defaulted. No address for the residence is documented in any source reached, and the pin is a generic Paris coordinate
stops.campa: The police come through his apartment. The stated cause is his support for Charlie Bauer, a former convict he had helped through rehabilitation work, and behind that stands a decade of Italian traffic. In the same twelve months La Borde is searched too, so that both his addresses are turned over inside one year, the flat and the château. He is forty-nine, a known name in three countries, and his papers are being carried out in boxes by men who will read them.

stops.name: Clinique de La Borde: the clinic searched
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year by the English-language entry on the clinic; the month is inferred and the day defaulted. Pin inherited byte-identical from gilles_deleuze.journey.json
stops.campa: A kidnapping investigation brings police up the drive at Cour-Cheverny to search a psychiatric clinic in which the patients keep the keys and put out the newspaper. La Borde has been an argument since 1953 that a hospital can be organized against its own tendency to turn into a prison. For one day it is searched like one. Oury and Guattari are twenty-six years into the experiment and it survives the visit; the clinic outlives them both and goes on staging a play every year with staff and patients in the cast.
suggested_refs: Nicolas Philibert, La Moindre des choses (1997), filmed at La Borde during the preparation of the annual play

stops.name: Éditions de Minuit: Mille Plateaux
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year of publication and the publisher; month and day defaulted. Pin inherited byte-identical from gilles_deleuze.journey.json
stops.campa: Volume two arrives eight years after volume one. Fifteen plateaus, each carrying a date, none requiring the one before it, so that the book can be entered anywhere and does not so much end as stop. The war machine, the refrain, the face, the smooth and the striated, becoming-animal: a vocabulary that geography, architecture, music theory and military staff colleges will still be borrowing from forty years later, mostly with the politics left out. Neither author ever says which sentence is whose, and they are asked constantly.
stops.quote: The two of us wrote Anti-Oedipus together. Since each of us was several, there was already quite a crowd. Here we have made use of everything that came within range, what was closest as well as farthest away.
stops.quote_source: Deleuze and Guattari, A Thousand Plateaus, trans. Brian Massumi (University of Minnesota Press, 1987), opening line of the Introduction. Verified verbatim against the Massumi PDF
suggested_refs: Mille Plateaux, Éditions de Minuit, 1980, first printing

stops.name: Paris, Radio Tomate and the comedian's candidacy
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year in both cases by French Wikipedia: the co-creation of Radio Tomate, and his support for Coluche's satirical presidential candidacy. Months and days defaulted. No studio address was reached and the pin is generic Paris
stops.campa: Mitterrand's election opens a legal space for private radio in France and Guattari builds a station into it at once, Radio Tomate. He has spent four years defending Italian pirates in French courts and now he holds a licence. The operation is the one he has always run: take an apparatus the professionals own, hand it to whoever turns up, and find out what comes out the other end. In the same months he backs Coluche, a comedian running for president as a joke that a million people take seriously enough to alarm the parties.
suggested_refs: Radio Tomate's broadcast records, Paris, from 1981

stops.name: São Paulo, the Brazilian tour
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The tour is recorded in the book Guattari made with Suely Rolnik, published in Portuguese as Micropolítica: Cartografias do Desejo (1986) and in English as Molecular Revolution in Brazil (Semiotext(e), 2008, not 2007 as commonly given). The city-by-city itinerary was not verified against any source fetched this session, so this stop is tagged reconstruction rather than attested, and the arrival date is approximate
stops.campa: He lands in Brazil with Suely Rolnik in the middle of the abertura, the slow unclenching of the dictatorship, and spends weeks in rooms full of people arguing about what to build next. Workers' Party militants, psychiatric reformers emptying the asylums, feminists, black movement organizers, squatters. He talks and is contradicted at length, on tape, and Rolnik keeps the recordings. The book that comes out of them four years later appears in Portuguese first. Brazil reads him before France has finished arguing about him.
suggested_refs: Guattari and Rolnik, Micropolítica: Cartografias do Desejo (Vozes, 1986); English as Molecular Revolution in Brazil (Semiotext(e), 2008)
A dated itinerary of the 1982 Brazilian tour
sources: Guattari and Rolnik, Molecular Revolution in Brazil, the published record of the trip

stops.name: Rio de Janeiro, the argument continues
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction, on the same footing as the São Paulo stop. Neither the order of the cities nor the dates within September are verified by any source fetched this session; the day is a placement, not an attestation
stops.campa: In Rio the argument goes on in front of different rooms. What he is putting is that a revolution conducted only at the scale of the party and the state will reproduce the state, and that the scale which decides things is the one where a hospital, a household or a neighbourhood association actually runs. Brazilian organizers push back with the observation that they are living under a dictatorship and do not have the option of skipping the state. The transcripts keep both halves of that exchange.
suggested_refs: The Rio sessions in Micropolítica: Cartografias do Desejo, for the transcripts of the exchanges
sources: Guattari and Rolnik, Molecular Revolution in Brazil

stops.name: Paris, getting Negri out
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year by English Wikipedia's 'Antonio Negri'; the month is inferred and the day defaulted. Negri was arrested on 7 April 1979, elected to the Italian parliament in June 1983, and left for France on claiming parliamentary immunity
stops.campa: Antonio Negri, four years in Italian custody on charges the prosecution keeps reshaping, is elected to parliament, walks out on immunity and crosses into France. Guattari is one of the people who makes the landing soft: papers, a place to be, Amnesty International, the network CINEL has been running since 1977. Negri stays in French exile fourteen years and France does not extradite him. Within two years the two of them have written a book together.

The Mitterrand doctrine on Italian political refugees

stops.name: Paris, Les nouveaux espaces de liberté and Les années d'hiver
stops.date_confidence: attested: Les nouveaux espaces de liberté, written in French with Antonio Negri, Paris, Dominique Bedou, 1985; Les années d'hiver: 1980-1985, Bernard Barrault, 1985. Months and days defaulted. Communists Like Us is the English edition, Semiotext(e), 1990, published in the United States; dating a Paris stop to 1990 conflates the two editions
stops.campa: Two books in one year. With Negri he writes Les nouveaux espaces de liberté, arguing that communism has to be rebuilt from the singular upward or not rebuilt at all. He is fifty-five and has published, organized or edited through every year the second title covers. Alone he publishes Les années d'hiver, and the title is not a description of a quiet stretch in his own life: it names the political weather of 1980 to 1985, the reaction closing across Europe while the left explains its defeat to itself.
suggested_refs: Les années d'hiver: 1980-1985 (Bernard Barrault, 1985)
Les nouveaux espaces de liberté (Dominique Bedou, 1985); English as Communists Like Us (Semiotext(e), 1990)

stops.date_confidence: reconstruction, and weak. No dedicated source page for a 1985 Japan trip was located or fetched this session; the year, the month and the city are all placements. stops.name: Paris, Cartographies schizoanalytiques
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year of publication; month and day defaulted. The pin is a generic Paris coordinate
stops.campa: Under his own name he sets out the apparatus at last: the four functors, the machinic phylum, existential territories, incorporeal universes, flows, and a way of diagramming how a subject is produced rather than discovered. The vocabulary is the one he had been using at the clinic since the fifties, where none of it counted as theory. The collaboration made him a famous name; this is the machinery the collaboration was assembled out of. It is his most technical book and his least read.
suggested_refs: Cartographies schizoanalytiques (Galilée, 1989), first edition

stops.name: Paris, Éditions Galilée: Les trois écologies
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year and for publication in Paris by Éditions Galilée; the month is inferred and the day defaulted. Gathered material anchored this publication to La Borde, which is a place error, and the thinking rather than the printing belongs to the clinic
stops.campa: A hundred pages arguing that the environment cannot be saved as an object, because it is not one. Three ecologies have to move together: the environmental, the social and the mental, the poisoned river and the broken union and the flattened subjectivity of a person in front of a television. He calls the joined discipline ecosophy. In 1989 it reads as an eccentric French extension of green politics. It is now the most cited thing he wrote alone, and the reason his name turns up in architecture schools.
suggested_refs: Les Trois Écologies (Galilée, 1989), first edition; English as The Three Ecologies, trans. Pindar and Sutton (Athlone, 2000)
sources: archive.org item 1989-felix-guattari-les-trois-ecologies, the French original read directly

stops.name: Éditions de Minuit: Qu'est-ce que la philosophie?
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year of publication and the publisher; month and day defaulted. Pin inherited byte-identical from gilles_deleuze.journey.json
stops.campa: The last book carrying both names. Philosophy creates concepts, science lays down functions, art builds blocs of sensation, and all three cut into chaos by means that do not substitute for one another. It is a calm book about what the two of them have been doing since 1969, written at the end of the doing, and Deleuze does most of the writing. Twenty-two years after Muyard put them in a room together, the joint signature stops. Guattari has a year and a half left.
suggested_refs: Qu'est-ce que la philosophie?, Éditions de Minuit, 1991, first edition
sources: gilles_deleuze.journey.json (Minuit pin; the stop on the last joint book)

stops.name: Paris, Éditions Galilée: Chaosmose
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year and for publication by Galilée in Paris; the month is inferred and the day defaulted. Gathered material placed the publication at Cour-Cheverny, which is wrong: only the year was right there
stops.campa: The last book he finishes, out from Galilée in Paris five months before his death. It asks how subjectivity is produced, by machines, by institutions, by works of art, and it refuses the humanist answer and the structuralist one in the same movement. Chaosmosis is his own word for the passage between chaos and a complexity that holds for a while before it goes back. He writes it at sixty-two, with the ecological argument and the clinical argument folded into each other.
suggested_refs: Chaosmose (Galilée, 1992), first edition; English as Chaosmosis, trans. Bains and Pefanis (Indiana, 1995)

stops.name: Clinique de La Borde: the heart attack
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day, place and cause by both language editions. The pin is the corrected value inherited byte-identical from gilles_deleuze.journey.json; two other pairs circulate for this site, 47.4926 / 1.4536 and 47.4808 / 1.4674, and both are wrong
stops.campa: He dies of a heart attack at La Borde on the twenty-ninth of August, sixty-two years old, in the building he first came to in 1955 and never really left. Thirty-seven years of rotas, accounts, seminars, the summer play, the standing argument about who counts as staff. The Paris of newspapers, courts, radios and publishers is a hundred and eighty kilometres north; the château is where he is when it happens. Both language editions give the day, the place and the cause.
suggested_refs: La Borde's own record of Guattari's death, 29 August 1992

stops.name: Paris, Le Monde diplomatique, October
stops.date_confidence: attested: 'Pour une refondation des pratiques sociales', Le Monde diplomatique, October 1992, pp. 26-27, the article page confirmed live at monde-diplomatique.fr. Day defaulted. The piece appears two months after his death
stops.campa: Two months after the heart attack a newspaper carries his argument to more readers than any of the books reached. He asks for a refoundation of social practices and puts the ecosophical case in a page and a half: mentalities do not change while the material and social surroundings stay as they are, which is why the three ecologies have to be worked at once or not at all. The sentence is now quoted everywhere as though it came from Les trois écologies. It did not. It came from here, after he was dead.
stops.quote: Yet, without modifications to the social and material environment, there can be no change in mentalities. Here, we are in the presence of a circle that leads me to postulate the necessity of founding an "ecosophy" that would link environmental ecology to social ecology and mental ecology.
stops.quote_source: Félix Guattari, 'Remaking Social Practices', trans. Sophie Thomas, revised by Brian Holmes, in The Guattari Reader, ed. Gary Genosko (Blackwell, 1996); originally 'Pour une refondation des pratiques sociales', Le Monde diplomatique, October 1992, pp. 26-27. Verified against the PDF at raumstation.cc. The widespread attribution of this passage to The Three Ecologies is wrong: the sentence is absent from the 1989 French original, checked directly
suggested_refs: Le Monde diplomatique, October 1992, pp. 26-27, the original article
The Guattari Reader, ed. Gary Genosko (Blackwell, 1996), for the published English wording
